title: These Mortal Joys, How Soon They Fade
description: These Mortal Joys, How Soon They Fade in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 525 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: These mor-tal joys, how soon they fade! How swift they pass a-way! The dy-ing flower re-clines its head, The beau-ty of a day.

lines: These mortal joys, how soon they fade!
The dying flower reclines its head,
Soon are those earthly treasures lost,
Scarce the possession can we boast,
When straight we find them gone.
But there are joys which cannot die,
With God laid up in store;
The seeds which piety and love
In the fair, fertile fields above

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
